item.title: Patrick Mahomes Ended a TD Drought as Chiefs Beat The Falcons
item.description: Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs had quite a day on Sunday. With Mahomes leading the attack, Kansas City took the Atlanta Falcons to the woodshed, showing the NFC South team what a real Super Bowl contender looks like. Mahomes had a game to remember against Atlanta, which struggled all game long to find a way to slow down the Chiefs at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta. The three-time Super Bowl champion quarterback threw not just one, not two, not three, not four but five touchdowns with zero interceptions on 22/35 pass completions. Mahomes was also well protected, as he was sacked just once for a loss of nine yards. Even without star running back Kenneth Walker III , who was ruled out before the game with an injury, Kansas City’s attack overpowered the host team. Emmett Johnson filled in nicely for Walker, with the rookie running back burning rubber for 101 rushing yards on 22 carries, while also adding 70 receiving yards and two scores on six receptions and seven targets. item.title: How Mizzou basketball woke up Jason Crowe Jr., pulled off comeback vs Marquette
item.description: CHICAGO — Jason Crowe Jr. was trying to pull a fast one on his head coach. With 13 minutes, 24 seconds left on the gameclock, after riding the bench for the previous four minutes while Missouri basketball tried to dig itself out of a double-digit hole, Crowe tried to slip past Dennis Gates while the coach was making substitutions. Gates, even with his team trailing by six points, was having nothing of the sort from his star freshman point guard. The head coach grabbed Crowe’s arm and sent him back to his seat. Crowe sat there for another two minutes. “He knew I called somebody else. His little behind wanted to get back in the game. He thought I was going to let him go, and I pulled him back. He wanted to get back in the game, but he needed to watch some things,” Gates said. … “He's just ready to play. He looks at me with little puppy dog eyes when I look down. … I pointed at one person, gave him the nod, and he just ran trying to get an opportunity to get back in the game.” Crowe’s time came, and he didn’t waste it. “That's his way of saying, ‘Coach, I'm ready to go,’” Gates said. Missouri basketball staged a remarkable comeback win over Marquette on Sunday at United Center, beating the Golden Eagles 69-64 after looking down and out for most of the neutral-site contest. More: Mizzou basketball erases big deficit, defeats Marquette as Crowe closes strong The Tigers trailed the Golden Eagles by 11 points in the second half. But they’ve got a five-star freshman to help with sticky situations like that. Crowe went from lethargic to lethal in the game’s closing stretch. One catch-and-shoot 3-point shot and, with 49 seconds remaining, a turn-and-shoot triple that gave the Tigers the lead for good. A contested mid-ranger. A backdoor cut into a layup, and-1. Nowhere was safe from the free-scoring freshman once he turned it on. He finished with 17 points. Of those, 13 came in the final six minutes and 30 seconds of the game. Quite the turnaround. Crowe opened the game 1-of-8 from the field. He had six turnovers. That bought him a sideline seat. “He was bulls—ing early, man. I told him that. At the end of the day, I'm not gonna sugarcoat it with him,” Gates said. “He was BSing, and we needed him to step up, grow up in-game, stop looking for whistles. And once he stopped looking for a referee to rescue him, he became a participant with his team, and he focused up and made the big plays that we knew he could make for us.” That, like Mizzou’s outstanding offensive burst to close the game after a grizzly 24 turnovers, came from somewhere in the general vicinity of nowhere. At the mention of the number ‘24’ postgame, Crowe closed his eyes and mouthed an F-word we can’t print. Indeed. Twenty-four turnovers is the most in any game since Gates has arrived in Columbia. The Tigers matched the previous high of Gates’ tenure, which was 21 in a December 2022 loss to Kansas, when there were more than seven minutes left in the game. And that was hardly the only issue. item.title: Fairbanks boys soccer rolls to OHSAA Division V state championship
item.description: In a showdown of two first-time boys soccer state finalists , central Ohio’s representative got its championship. Fairbanks thoroughly dominated the Division V final Nov. 15 at ScottsMiracle-Gro Field , getting goals from its top two offensive threats – sophomore forward Ty Schroeder and senior midfielder Kaden Procuniar – in a 4-0 win over Creston Norwayne that did not always feel that close. Fairbanks (22-2), just a year removed from its first district and regional titles, had the first 14 shots of the game and ultimately outshot Norwayne 28-2. Schroeder scored his team-leading 34th goal in the bottom center of the net with 32:15 left on the Panthers’ 13th shot of the game. Three minutes later, Procuniar netted his 11th goal of the year. He also finished with 21 assists. Senior forward Nolan Baker added the final two goals 30 seconds apart with less than seven minutes to go. Fairbanks, the first Union County program to win a state title, finished the season on a 14-game winning streak. The Panthers outscored their opponents 90-12. Norwayne (17-5-1) did not muster a shot until the 49th minute, when Lysander Bauman’s try was stopped by senior goalie Drew Sorg. That was Sorg’s only save of the game. Norwayne’s Garrett Ponting stopped seven shots. This story will be updated . High school sports reporter Dave Purpura can be reached at dpurpura@dispatch.com and at @dp_dispatch on X. item.title: ‘Ultimate pro since day one’… Dianna Russini praises NFL star after ’emotional’ postgame interview
item.description: Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images Returning NFL insider Dianna Russini has paid tribute to the man behind the biggest story in the league in Week 10 – Kirk Cousins. With the Minnesota Vikings’ season at risk of collapse, the team made an SOS trade for their former quarterback Kirk Cousins at the deadline, sending a 2027 third-round pick to the Raiders. Cousins made a winning return to the Vikings – leading the team to a 30-10 win over NFC North rivals the Green Bay Packers. The 38-year-old quarterback fought back tears in his postgame interview, expressing his happiness at making a successful return to the team. He was praised by NFL personality Dianna Russini, who wrote on X: “Kirk has been the ultimate pro since day one in the league. “Seeing him get emotional after that win tells you everything about what this game still means to him. Great story.” What Kirk Cousins said after Vikings win Kirk Cousins was relieved to get the road win at Lambeau Field, and reminded the world why this game was a deeply personal one – as it was where his Vikings career came to an end. He said: “It was emotional coming to the stadium. Three years ago, tearing my Achilles here, it’s been a tough three years and I was just grateful for the opportunity to play here today. “Grateful for my teammates and what they did today to make this outcome possible. It’s been a tough three years.” He added of his Vikings comeback: “There’s more to this story being written.” The victory takes the Vikings to 7-2, stopping a two-game losing streak. And in the process, it was the most dangerous the team has looked all year. Nobody would begrudge Cousins his moment. item.title: Mizzou women’s basketball holds off Lindenwood, improves to 5-0
item.description: Lindenwood opened its trip to Mizzou Arena with a 5-0 run. But the Tigers shut down any chance of an upset, using an 11-2 sprint of its own to bury the Lions. Mizzou held the lead the rest of the way, downing Lindenwood 79-63 and improving to 5-0 on the season. Both teams had the offense rolling early, but the Tigers held a 25-20 edge at the end of the first quarter. The Tigers were extremely efficient in the quarter, shooting 62.5% from the field and 50% from 3. Abbey Schreacke hit back-to-back 3-pointers for six early points. Khloe Ford also recorded six points in the opening frame. But Grace Slaughter led all scorers with nine points, shooting 4-5 from the field and a perfect 1-1 from three while playing all 10 minutes. From there, Lindenwood never got any closer. Mizzou started the second quarter on an 8-3 run, extending the lead out to 10. The Lions gave themselves a chance with less than three minutes to go in the fourth quarter, cutting the deficit down to nine. But the Tigers squashed any dreams of a comeback, holding their opponents scoreless for the final 2:44 of the game. “We went a few stretches offensively without scoring, but to me, the defense is what kept us ahead and kept us in charge of the game,” Mizzou coach Kellie Harper said. Slaughter added another six points in the fourth quarter, becoming a key contributor at both the start and end of the win. She led the team with 21 points, grabbing seven rebounds while shooting 8-14 from the field and 2-5 on 3-pointers. “I think our coaches really encourage us to rim run, play fast,” Slaughter said. “Our guards do a great job of hitting us in transition, and it is a lot of fun to play fast … they do a great job of helping me be in positions where I can be versatile, whether that’s on the perimeter shooting 3s or being able to find a mismatch inside and get a post up.” Slaughter moved into 10th place on the all-time scoring list, now up to 1,552 for her career. Next up is ninth-place Evan Unrau at 1,597. I’d expect Slaughter to catch her sometime within the next three games. “I’m just really thankful to get to play for Mizzou, but then on top of that, just play for a team that really cares for each other and a coaching staff that really pours into us and really helps us be successful on and off the court,” Slaughter said. “I wouldn’t be here if it weren’t for them.” Another key contribution came from Neveah Caffey, who scored 12 points and totalled a career-high seven assists. Denver Broncos tight end Evan Engram was reportedly among the players considered as the NFC contender searched for additional receiving help . San Francisco’s interest in Engram reflected a need that extended beyond its wide receiver room. The 49ers were looking for dependable pass catchers who could help quarterback Brock Purdy while injuries affected the team’s offensive options. A tight end capable of working across the formation would have offered another way to create mismatches and keep the passing attack productive. The 49ers ultimately chose a different route by acquiring Allen from the Indianapolis Colts. item.title: England stun world champions Spain in one of their greatest victories
item.description: Anthony Gordon (from left), Jude Bellingham and Morgan Rogers celebrate a historic victory - Uefa via Getty Images/David Ramos Thomas Tuchel may not have planned it this way, but in one night he gave us all the rich history of the England team at once: some glorious attacking football, some self-sabotage defending, a red card, a late siege and a fight. This was the beguiling story of Spain 2 England 3, an evening that began with the world champions parading the World Cup trophy and ended with 10 Englishmen defending a lead with their last breath. England beat the world champions in Madrid, and for more than 30 minutes including injury time they did so with 10 men, Dan Burn heading the last ball out as per the tradition of a defensive rearguard action. This was the game that had it all: including a substitute, in Djed Spence, who had already picked up a yellow card on the bench before he came on. It was a coming-of-age performance in goal for James Trafford . So too for Ben White, the 2022 World Cup departee who scored the third and lunged with astonishing effect in the 84th minute to block a Nico Williams shot. Trafford again! 👊🏻An excellent double save from the Leeds United keeper 🙌 https://t.co/L27oQFQO1J — ITV Football (@itvfootball) November 15, 2026 This was a performance good enough to win a World Cup final, never mind Nations League Group A3 – just a shame England neglected to get to that World Cup final in the summer. The fight in question was at half-time as the players came off and White and Fabián Ruiz first tangled and others dived in. There was so much to admire. England began the night testing Spain’s first-phase passing to breaking point. They began the second half counter-attacking Spain for two goals from Ezri Konsa and White. Then after Elliot Anderson’s red card, this was a different England. With Trafford in inspired form, they held off the relentless Spain for long enough. Harry Kane scored his 93rd England goal from the spot and was replaced before the end so that Myles Lewis-Skelly’s energy could give the midfield one more lease of life. By the end, the excitement meant that Kane was unable to take his seat on the bench, and he stood alongside Tuchel in the technical area, cajoling and advising. England have beaten Spain on Spanish territory in recent times, but it was the nature of this performance, its many qualities when the moment required them, that made it so significant. This was the end of a 43-game unbeaten streak for the European and world champions, and it was ended by an England team in their best form in recent years. item.title: Teenager Andreeva caps stunning week with WTA Finals title
item.description: Mirra Andreeva is the third teenager to win the WTA Finals singles trophy on debut at the tournament [Getty Images] For Mirra Andreeva, the thought of her first WTA Finals singles campaign was so stressful that it gave her "a little breakdown" in a practice session before the tournament. The 19-year-old may have been nervous on arrival at Indian Wells, but she leaves California as the champion, having been the standout player of the week. The French Open winner produced a hard-fought 7-5 6-3 victory over Elina Svitolina in Sunday's final to become the youngest champion of the event in 22 years. The Russian has now risen to second in the world rankings - and she will start the 2027 season just 293 points behind top-ranked Elena Rybakina. Andreeva did not drop a set on her way to the title and lost only 26 games across her five matches. She raised her arms in celebration after beating Svitolina before racing to celebrate with her team, which includes 1994 Wimbledon champion Conchita Martinez. "I am super thankful to my team for pushing me to my limits, for forcing me to do stuff when I don't want to do anything," Andreeva said. "Thanks for fighting with me, thanks for forcing me to do everything that I have to do and not asking any questions!" As well as £2.55m in prize money, Andreeva also won a custom purple Mercedes - and joked she was happy to remain a "passenger princess" until she passed her test. Andreeva thanks herself again after stellar season Mirra Andreeva is the youngest WTA Finals champion since a 17-year-old Maria Sharapova in 2004 [Getty Images] One of the most notable parts of Andreeva's performance has been her increased maturity. In March, she swore at the Indian Wells crowd after suffering an early defeat in the venue's WTA Tour tournament, and she has struggled to control her emotions on court in the past. However, she showed little sign of that during this tournament. Against Svitolina, one of the grittiest players on the women's tour, she lost a break lead three times across the two sets. Each time, she reset admirably, upping her aggression on her backhand in particular to put pressure back on her opponent. After losing serve in a mammoth nine-minute game in the second set, Andreeva marched back to her chair and then broke Svitolina from 40-0 down in the next game to stay in front. While her serve was not at its best, Andreeva still saved nine of the 12 break points she faced and hit 19 winners to Svitolina's 10. "This fighting mindset helped me to get more brave and aggressive in the important moments," Andreeva told Sky Sports. "This is just a dream. I had a little breakdown in my practice just before Indian Wells because I was so stressed. "I didn't want to lose a match in the group. It's amazing." The 35-year-old started Sunday's final round of The Annika with a one-shot lead and two late birdies saw her claim victory. Duncan, who joined the tour in 2014, had only enjoyed one top-10 finish this season. But her three-under-par 67 saw her finish on 16 under at Pelican Golf Club in Belleair, Florida, two shots clear of her nearest challenger, South Korea's Choi Hye-jin . "I got so many people to thank that believed in me when I wasn't sure if I wanted to keep playing or if I was good enough to keep playing," Duncan said followng her win. "To be here, I'm just completely shocked." Duncan was tied for the lead with Choi with two holes left to play before her late heroics. "Coming into today I kind of thought, 'No matter what happens I learned a huge lesson,' and hopefully I can take that forward with me," Duncan said. item.title: Wilson survives Wakelin comeback for third title
item.description: Kyren Wilson won the World Championship in 2024 [Getty Images] Kyren Wilson survived a stunning late comeback from Chris Wakelin to win the Champion of Champions tournament in Leicester. Wilson, 34, looked to be cruising to victory with a 9-3 lead and needed just one more frame for victory, but a determined Wakelin fought back in the evening session to put himself in touching distance at 9-8. Wakelin's impressive breaks of 131, 57 and 50 put Wilson on notice but he held his nerve for a 10-8 win with his fourth century break of the day. The win extends Wilson's fine run of form as he sealed his third consecutive title after triumphs at the Northern Ireland Open and the International Championship . He started confidently, taking control with a 135 break in the opening frame, and surged into a 4-0 lead before Wakelin recovered to make it 4-3. Wilson then notched five frames in a row and had the title in his sights before Wakelin started his response to set up the thrilling finale. "I made hard work of that in the end, didn't I?" Wilson told ITV after his victory. "Full respect to Chris, he really dug in there well. I played some good stuff and felt I had killed the match in the first session. "I've never felt so exhausted, I'm so drained. I felt so much pressure to get over the line." It is Wilson's first Champion of Champions win, having previously reached the final in 2018 where he lost to seven-time world champion Ronnie O'Sullivan. He is also the first player to win three tournaments in a row since Judd Trump in 2023.

item.title: Underwood seeks better communication ahead of Duke matchup
item.description: CHAMPAIGN, Ill. — Two Illinois freshmen, Ethan Brown and Quentin Coleman, were a disruptive force on defense against Sam Houston. Of Illinois’ nine steals in the 108-86 win, the duo accounted for seven. Brown racked up three while Coleman grabbed four, the third time in four games either had two or more steals. However, Brad Underwood wasn’t thrilled with their performance; not because of the stats, but rather the lack of communication. “It’s a challenge right now, from my seat, with communication,” Underwood said. “I cannot get this group to talk.” The head coach said Tomislav Ivisic, David Mirkovic and Jake Davis are the three best communicators on the team. With two of them out for the foreseeable future, it could make things more difficult down the road, and it’s already impacting the defense now. It hasn’t happened yet, but Underwood needs his young players, like Brown and Coleman, to step up. At the moment, though, they aren’t speaking up, mainly because they don’t know how. Underwood made a point of acting out his younger players’ tendencies, which he said are either sitting on their phones or playing video games. “I’m amazed that they know the ABCs and how to speak English,” Underwood said. Brad Underwood on freshman communication issues four games into the season 😅🏀 #Illini pic.twitter.com/1DDcGpAUx3 — The Champaign Room (@Champaign_Room) November 14, 2026 Underwood said the lack of communication has led to fundamental mistakes. Against Cincinnati, Brown got beat on a cut, and while Underwood made it a teaching moment, Brown didn’t recognize the same play against Sam Houston. Underwood said part of the reason why these younger players don’t talk is that they never have. “They’ve never been asked to talk before,” Underwood said. “Now it’s our job to help them know what to say.” While it ultimately didn’t hurt them against the Bearkats, it certainly could down the line. Bigger and better teams are around the corner — Duke, for instance — and it won’t be so easy to bounce back from a missed assignment on defense. Duke is one of the better teams in the nation in offensive rebounding. Allowing the Blue Devils to attack those defensive breakdowns and get second-chance points could mean another early-season ranked loss for the Illini. And if they can’t fix it early, it could mean more losses down the road. “I’ve said it a million times, and I’ve got at least another three or four million left in me; quiet teams lose,” Underwood said. It’s unlikely that Illinois figures out this problem in the first two weeks of the season. It probably won’t figure it out in the four weeks. However, once it does, the Illini could have a defense to match its offense. With how productive many of the freshmen have been on defense, it wouldn’t be surprising to see a jump in the overall quality of the defense later in the season. Illinois just has to keep getting louder.

item.title: Falcons’ Michael Penix Jr. Drops Bijan Robinson Warning
item.description: The Atlanta Falcons were smoked by the Kansas City Chiefs, 35-13, on Sunday afternoon, dropping them to 3-7 on the season. The Falcons managed 370 yards of total offense on the day, but they only reached the end zone once, which came from a rushing touchdown by running back Bijan Robinson. Robinson carried the ball 16 times for 71 yards in the loss. He also caught four passes for six yards. Quarterback Michael Penix Jr. does not think 20 touches are enough for Atlanta’s star halfback, and he said as much after the game in what appeared to be a warning to Kevin Stefanski and the coaching staff. “We’ve got to get him the ball more,” Penix said . Atlanta Falcons need more Bijan Robinson Nov 15, 2026; Atlanta, Georgia, USA; Kansas City Chiefs linebacker Drue Tranquill (23) prepares to make a tackle on Atlanta Falcons running back Bijan Robinson (7) during the second quarter at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images Robinson leads the NFL with 951 rushing yards this season, averaging 5.1 yards per carry while scoring six touchdowns on the ground. He has also hauled in 35 receptions for 256 yards and a score. But apparently, it isn’t enough for the Falcons. Atlanta entered Sunday ranking in the bottom half of the NFL in yards per game and points per game, which is rather inexcusable for a team with weapons like Robinson, Drake London and Kyle Pitts aboard. Penix has been a bit inconsistent under center, but he hasn’t played terribly, so the Falcons’ lack of offense is a bit of a mystery. Atlanta is still alive in the NFC South race, but that’s only because of the ineptitude of the division. It’s clear this is not a good football team, and while more Robinson would help, it wouldn’t be the sole answer. item.title: Record alert! Kagiso Rabada surpasses Allan Donald in South Africa’s all-time wicket tally
item.description: Kagiso Rabada added another milestone to his illustrious career on Sunday, surpassing legendary fast bowler Allan Donald to become South Africa’s fourth-highest wicket-taker in international cricket. However, the landmark moment was followed by a spirited Bangladesh fightback on the opening day of the first Test. Rabada claimed five wickets for 51 runs to take his international tally across Tests, ODIs and T20Is to 606, moving past Donald's 602. Shaun Pollock leads the South African charts with 823 wickets, followed by Dale Steyn (697) and Makhaya Ntini (661). The 31-year-old also registered his 18th five-wicket haul in Test cricket, drawing level with Ntini for joint-third place on South Africa's all-time list. Donald is second with 20 five-fors, while Steyn leads the standings with 26. Rabada strikes early as Bangladesh lose top order Rabada made an immediate impact, striking twice in the opening exchanges as Bangladesh endured a difficult start. Debutant Mahfijul Islam fell for a first-ball duck, while Mominul Haque also departed without scoring. The fast bowler then produced a superb delivery to dismiss Bangladesh captain Najmul Hossain Shanto, leaving the visitors reeling at 22/3. Tanzid Hasan and Towhid Hridoy attempted to stabilise the innings with a valuable partnership. Tanzid scored 67 before Rabada returned after lunch to remove him and Mushfiqur Rahim in quick succession, completing his five-wicket haul. Bangladesh were struggling at 121/5, but the contest took a dramatic turn thereafter. Hridoy, Litton script remarkable recovery Hridoy found an able partner in Litton Das as the duo turned the innings around with an unbroken sixth-wicket stand of 206 runs, the highest partnership by a Bangladesh pair against South Africa in their Test encounters. Hridoy produced a magnificent 137 off 208 deliveries, registering his maiden Test century against South Africa. He became only the second Bangladesh batter to score a Test hundred against the Proteas after Mahmudul Hasan Joy in 2022. Litton, meanwhile, remained unbeaten on 92 as Bangladesh finished the opening day at 327/6, recovering from a precarious position to take control of the innings.
